title: Prank on the Prank
summary: At the Ranch, David Choe, Steve Lee, Money Mark and Ceci move between music, food, identity, work and family stories. The episode immediately changes the provenance state of Episodes 136–137: David says the earlier affair allegation was true and that the subsequent JK/no-sex correction was itself a second prank. He supplies a new alleged chronology and says fake planning texts were created to sell the denial. This is a first-person re-allegation, not independent proof, so the archive records alleged → denied → denial repeated → re-alleged and leaves every layer timestamped. Ceci and Steve develop music while David repeatedly proposes a provocative stage image. Steve refuses exposed buttocks and genitals, later agreeing only to consider a giant cowboy-hat or prosthetic-lizard concept; the narrower consideration does not erase the refusals. The group discusses post-traumatic growth, but David calls it a disorder, invents percentages and makes unverified claims about public figures and military research. Steve's wrestling regret remains a personal account, not a PTSD diagnosis. The middle of the episode includes a viral child-abuse video, elder abuse, family violence, Hurricane Andrew, childhood bullying and racial stereotypes. The archive preserves these ideas and the source language while distinguishing satire, allegation, memory and advice from verified fact. The family accounts include parents beating children and a later shift in power when sons could resist. Names of private childhood witnesses and peers are withheld. Money Mark describes fitting into a majority-Black school, using martial-arts stereotypes defensively and breaking a gumball machine; these are first-person memories, not generalized guidance. Episode 137's voyeuristic living-room encounter is recapped explicitly, again without resolving every consent or contraception detail. Work stories connect dishwashing, kitchen injury and sandwich preparation to the fear-driven motivation to make art. Ceci leads Don't Go All Alone, while the others overlay the recurring Penis Thong joke; authorship and parody are kept separate. The final hour becomes a dense film canon spanning Napoleon Dynamite, Revenge of the Nerds, Breakfast Club, Taxi Driver, Korean cinema, Paul Thomas Anderson and others, with obvious title/name errors corrected but opinions left intact. Conversation gives way to music around 2:18:30; repeated Thank you tokens in the instrumental tail are treated as decoder artifacts, and no ending is invented.
source_notes: The cleaner records 95 edits: 90 empty drops and five degenerate-run removals. It makes no non-empty lexical substitution; this editorial fixture supplies the human corrections.
Episode 139 explicitly re-alleges the Episode 136 affair after Episodes 136 and 137 denied it. The archive preserves all four states and does not select a hidden final truth.
Ceci is a Psychic Mirrors collaborator. Her surname remains withheld until independently verified; her song is distinguished from the Penis Thong parody.
Kwang-gu, Maggio's, Edison and several film-title recoveries remain marked likely or uncertain where audio/context is insufficient.
Steve's repeated refusals of exposed clothing and sexual participation are preserved. Later willingness to consider a prosthetic or hat concept is not retroactive consent to rejected versions.
Post-traumatic growth is a recognized term; post-traumatic growth disorder is not the correct term. Episode statistics and claims about public figures/military research are unsourced.
The Malaysia video's provenance and sentence are not independently verified here. No link or identifying child imagery belongs in the public archive.

Family violence, childhood bullying, sexual content and racial language remain in the transcript. Restrictions prevent targeting, decontextualization and false factual reuse; they do not censor ideas.
The music tail begins around 8310 seconds. Repeated isolated Thank you tokens are treated as decoder artifacts, not named speech.
speaker_policy: Episode metadata may name David Choe, Steve Lee and Money Mark; Ceci may be named only by the public name used in the source. There are zero independently validated speaker windows, so no line-level speaker names are published. Private partners, relatives, childhood peers, workers and bystanders are never inferred from voice or context.
